compatibility.policy: This registry is the single source of truth for the hand-written SDK layers (transport, session, entitlement, preferences, runtime). It covers what ops/build/sdk-surface.json deliberately does not: the operationId surface is generated for TypeScript and Python only, so the hosted-login and commercial-entitlement behaviour of every published SDK is reconciled here instead. The checker never infers a capability from source; every present entry names the exact file and symbol that provides it, and every missing entry names the wave that will add it. A capability declared as parity must be present in every language, so closing a gap means flipping an entry from missing to present with a real symbol, not relaxing the declaration. Capability entries are append-only in id; changing the file or symbol behind a present entry is a deliberate edit the diff gate can review, and dropping an id or downgrading parity from parity to divergent is a breaking change for the cross-language contract and requires a minor version bump plus a CHANGELOG entry. Adding a language id is allowed and must declare every existing capability for it. A language is onboarded only after it has been reviewed against the parity floor; a language still onboarding must declare every capability so its debt is reported rather than hidden, but is not held to parity until it is onboarded. This exists so a newly added SDK is neither able to fake a pass nor able to downgrade a capability to turn the gate green. A capability may only become present in a language by implementing it in that language's SDK, never by a consumer reaching past the SDK to call the endpoint itself.

capabilities.summary: The HTTP transport is an injectable seam so a caller can supply retries, proxies, timeouts, or a test double.

python.note: W4: the seam is emitted by cmd/gensdk, so the generated client and the hosted-login facade share it. The default UrllibTransport refuses redirects, so a credential endpoint can never replay an authorization code, refresh token, or bearer at another host.

rust.note: W4: async Transport is the default; ReqwestTransport uses reqwest async, and the optional blocking feature adapts reqwest through spawn_blocking.

kotlin.plan: W5 generator coverage does not apply. OAuthTransport and its OAuthTokenResponse wire type are both module-internal, so closing this means deciding which wire types are consumer API; it is a design change, not a one-file edit.

capabilities.summary: The short-lived login transaction is persisted through a caller-suppliable store so multi-worker deployments are possible.

kotlin.note: The seam carries the transaction, token, and activation records as opaque strings, so the record encoding and per-configuration key derivation stay in the client. AndroidSecureStore remains the default, so SnaplinkAuthClient(context, configuration) is unchanged; secure record writes and reads for a restart, per-configuration isolation, and storage faults failing closed are covered by sdks/kotlin/test/SecureStoreTest.kt.

capabilities.summary: Callers can branch on a usable session without issuing a request.

kotlin.note: A local point-in-time read only: no refresh, no request, no write, and no delete, so it can neither create nor resurrect a session. It shares one freshness predicate with accessToken(), so false at or inside the 60-second refresh skew means accessToken() would have to reach the network. Stricter than Go's IsLoggedIn, which ignores expiry. An unreadable record raises secure_storage_error instead of answering false, and the no-network, no-write, skew-boundary, and in-flight-logout cases are covered by sdks/kotlin/test/SessionQueryTest.kt.

swift.plan: W5 generator coverage does not apply; see the swift SDK roadmap. Callers infer it from accessToken().

capabilities.summary: Local token state is dropped without notifying the authorization server.

kotlin.note: A local-only reset: it drops the token set, the pending transaction, and the pending activation without contacting Snaplink. logout() remains the revoking path. Covered by SnaplinkAuthClientTest.clearDropsLocalSessionAndPendingTransactionWithoutRevocation, which asserts revokeCount stays 0.

swift.plan: W5 generator coverage does not apply; see the swift SDK roadmap. logout() revokes and clears; there is no local-only reset.
swift.note: logout() revokes and clears; there is no local-only reset.

capabilities.summary: A signed commercial entitlement file is verified locally so an air-gapped deployment can gate paid features without a vendor call on the login path.

go.note: W2: crypto/ed25519 is stdlib, so verification is direct rather than injected. A structurally incomplete envelope reports license_malformed, not a zero-valued version, to match the other SDKs.

typescript.note: W2: verification is async so a WebCrypto or @noble/curves verifier can be injected without this package taking a dependency; WebCrypto Ed25519 is still unevenly deployed.

python.note: W2: the package is stdlib-only by design and the stdlib has no Ed25519, so a LicenseVerifier callable is injected (cryptography, PyNaCl, or equivalent) rather than adding a dependency or hand-rolling a signature check.

php.note: W2: a callable verifier is supplied; sodiumVerifier() uses ext-sodium when loaded so the package declares no hard extension requirement.

rust.note: W2: local Ed25519 verification. LicenseTrust::vendor_pinned() reports TrustUnconfigured until a release supplies the vendor root, so no placeholder key ships.

kotlin.symbol: public fun verify(raw: String, trust: SnaplinkLicenseTrust?): SnaplinkLicenseFile
kotlin.note: Local Ed25519 envelope version 1 verification with no network on any path. The trust root is always caller-supplied, so no vendor key ships; the declared algorithm and version are checked before any signature work, and Android exposes Ed25519 only from API 33, below which verification fails closed with license_verifier_unavailable rather than skipping the check. Driven against ops/build/sdk-conformance/license_file.json by LicenseFileConformanceTest.
